newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops, rebels locked in battle in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops, rebels locked in battle in north.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists launched a fierce attack on Sri Lankan troops advancing north along one flank as part of a major thrust into rebel territory on Thursday, military officials said.

Troops which advanced from the northern frontline town of Puvarasankulam met stiff resistance from Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at Kuruvikulam, west of the government-held town of Vavuniya, on Thursday morning, they said.
"There is heavy fighting going on in and around Kuruvikulam," one official in the north told Reuters.
At least 12 rebels were killed and more were believed wounded, he said, adding he was unsure of army casualties.
Meanwhile, troops which advanced on another flank to capture the rebel-held town of Omanthai on Wednesday, were consolidating, the Defence Ministry said on Thursday.

LTTE transmissions monitored by troops said at least 22 rebels had been killed and more than 25 wounded in the fresh offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", which was launched on Tuesday, a ministry statement said.
Army casualties stood at seven dead and 24 wounded, it said.
Unconfirmed reports from the north said around 19 people, which included soldiers and a few civilians, had been killed and about 45 soldiers wounded in the three-day-old offensive.

LTTE rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.

Analysts said the aim of the fresh offensive was to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north. Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops were heading.
An LTTE statement received by Reuters on Thursday said thousands of civilians have been forced to abandon their homes and take refuge in nearby jungles as troops advanced.
"MI24 helicopters and tanks are smashing everything," the statement said.
LTTE positions in the mainly scrub Wanni region came under heavy attack on Thursday when the army fired shells from bases at Welioya, Killinochichi and Elephant Pass in the north, officials said.
"The LTTE retaliated by shelling the Welioya camp, wounding three soldiers and killing one homeguard," a military official said.
"Yesterday there was severe confrontation. We hammered them hard and we expect high casualties on their side," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters.
Military officials said two army tanks were damaged in fighting on Wednesday after troops captured Omanthai town, along the strategic Jaffna-Vavuniya north-south highway.
The town fell after troops backed by helicopter gunships, artillery and tanks broke out of bases in Vavuniya in a largely unopposed thrust into the rebel heartland.
Omanthai constituted the southern forward defences of the LTTE, who control swathes of land further north.
